# Sizing a power station for a fridge

**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a station with about **1,000 Wh** for roughly half a day to a day, or **2,000 Wh** if you want 1.5 days or more. It also needs a surge rating of at least **1,300 W** and a pure sine wave inverter.

## The three checks

1. **Continuous watts:** A full-size fridge runs at roughly 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class station clears this ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** The compressor's startup spike is typically 1,000-2,400 W for a full-size fridge. A station with plenty of battery can still trip at startup if its surge rating is too low, so this is the spec that most often rules a unit out ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so average use is far below the running watts.

## Watt-hours by outage length

Estimates for average fridge use vary by source:

- **About 41 W average** (18 cu ft ENERGY STAR model): about 1,400 Wh per day, including inverter losses and headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- **About 60-70 W average** (a less efficient fridge): that would roughly double the runtime math above.

| Outage | Rough capacity |
|---|---|
| 8-12 hours | ~700-1,000 Wh |
| 24 hours | ~1,400-2,000 Wh |
| 2 days | ~2,800 Wh or more |

To be precise, check your fridge's EnergyGuide label. Average watts = kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760. A plug-in energy meter also works. Keep the door shut during the outage, since door openings and a warm kitchen raise real-world use.

## Options

- **~1,000 Wh class:** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (about 1,070 Wh) is estimated to run a fridge about 17 hours ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). The Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W AC, 2,700 W peak) is another pick ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)). I don't have direct purchase links for these from the results.
- **~2,000 Wh class (best for a full day or more):**
  - [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l): 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W continuous, 3,600 W surge, expandable up to 8 kWh. It's $899, and code AFF5OFF took $44.95 off in a cart test dated 2026-10-21. Estimated fridge runtime is about 33 hours. This is an affiliate link, so the retailer pays a commission at no cost to you.
  - [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W output, 3,000 W peak, listed at $699.99 after coupon. This link goes to Anker's guide page, which has the shop link.

Runtime figures are estimates. Confirm your fridge's startup draw against the station's surge rating before you buy.

If you tell me your fridge's size or EnergyGuide kWh/year and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this to one pick.
